title: Run the story-notes frontend checks at the mounted boundary

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: held notes answer across mounted cases

**Verdict: Insufficient evidence.** The fault was not shown to make the next case open with anything other than default answers, or to receive a late update, reproducibly. The literal suggested fault (end held answers before unmounting) changes no behavior. A stronger version delivers the held notes answer into the ending case's still-mounted board, which the scratch witness saw. The next-case promise failed in only 1 of 7 faulted runs and in 0 of 7 restored runs.

**Next proof action:** Find out whether the single faulted failure was caused by the fault. In it, the next case's banner went from `data-connection="awaiting"` to `"disconnected"` after `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)`. To check, repeat the faulted `mounted-dashboard` pair until the flip reproduces, and trace where the connection state comes from. If no fault can make a held answer reach the next case, record that the promise holds by construction. Two facts point that way: notes state lives per App (`useMemo` in `dashboard/src/storyNotes.ts`), and a held fetch belongs to the root that has already been unmounted.

## Story and revision
- Story: `.planning/seeds/SEED-404-run-dashboard-frontend-checks-at-doughnut-speed.md#run-the-remaining-dashboard-frontend-checks-at-doughnut-speed`, plan `.planning/slice-plans/707-run-story-notes-checks-at-the-mounted-boundary/PLAN.md` (slice 1 proof: "the next case ... opens the board with default answers and receives no late update").
- Revision: 7740fc354ff8f89eb2a8de63243792950fd6c6d8, in a detached scratch worktree. It was clean before the probe and was removed after restoration was verified.
- Promise: one case ends while a notes answer is still held, and the next case in the same file opens with default answers and no late update. Every case starts from a fresh mount.

## Faults (in `dashboard/test-support/mounted-dashboard/mountedDashboard.ts`, the `onTestFinished` cleanup in `joinMountedCase`)
- **Fault A (as suggested):** move `endHeldAnswers()` from the `finally` to before the teardown loop. **Result: no behavior change.** The maintained command passed 13 of 13 mounted cases (14 selected). The witness saw no late note in the mounted board. The reason is that ending a hold only resolves or rejects a promise, and the answer reaches the app in later microtasks. The first teardown's `unmount()` runs synchronously before those microtasks, so the board is already gone. Reordering alone is not a behavior-relevant fault. The ordering risk the retrospective named is real only if there is an `await` between ending a hold and unmounting.
- **Fault B (strengthened):** `await actSettled(() => endHeldAnswers());` before the teardown loop. This lets held answers settle into the still-mounted board.

## Maintained checks examined
- `dashboard/frontend-tests/mounted-dashboard.mounted.spec.ts`. Case :10 holds `storyNotesEndpoint` through the `held` paths option, which is ended by rejecting. Case :16 asserts `answersStillHeld()` is `[]` and `container.innerHTML` stays unchanged after `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)`. The guard in `mountAnsweredDashboard` throws "Answers held by an earlier case".
- `stories/story-notes-*.mounted.spec.ts`. The only `holdNext` user, `story-notes-refresh` :42, releases its hold before the case ends. **No maintained story-notes case ends with a `holdNextNotes` hold still kept,** so maintained proof never exercises the stale-delivery path (`holdNextNotes` ends by releasing the answer, not rejecting).

## Independent witness (scratch `stories/zz-ic-witness.mounted.spec.ts`, deleted)
- Case 1: mount `mountStoryNotesBoard("no notes")` and open notes on the Done card. `setNotes` a note "IC late note", then `holdNext()`, `runFor(checkIntervalMs)` and await `received`. The held body therefore carries the late note. Then register a MutationObserver on `#root` that records the late note appearing while the root is connected, and end the case without releasing.
- Case 2: mount the board again, assert `innerHTML` is unchanged after `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)`, and assert no late note was seen.
- Baseline: late-note-in-mounted-board=false, 2 of 2 passed. Fault A: false, 2 of 2 passed. **Fault B: true.** The stale notes answer reached the ending case's still-mounted board, so the observer fired. Case 2's own `innerHTML` stayed stable, and it failed only on the cross-case `seen` flag. The wrong behavior is confined to the ending case. The next case opened clean in this single witness run.

## Run observations (command: `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_FRONTEND_PROOF_RECORD=<file> npm run --silent test:dashboard:frontend -- mounted-dashboard stories/story-notes`, Node 24.21.0)
- Every proof record showed `selectedCount` 14 and `phase` completed: 13 mounted cases plus the Playwright `story-notes.spec.ts` attached-terminal case. This confirms the isolation pair and every story-notes case were reached.
- Baseline: 13 of 13 passed (exit 0).
- Fault A: 13 of 13 passed.
- Fault B: the first run failed `mounted-dashboard.mounted.spec.ts:16` at `expect(dashboard.container.innerHTML).toBe(opened)`. The only difference was the banner going from `data-connection="awaiting"` to `"disconnected"`. The next 6 faulted runs (B2 to B7) all passed 13 of 13. That is 1 failure in 7. Nothing connects the flip causally to the held notes answer, and the witness's next case under the same fault stayed stable.
- Restored: 6 runs (R, R2 to R6) all passed 13 of 13. Together with the baseline, 7 unfaulted runs passed. Load averages were 8 to 11 on the machine throughout.
- Restoration: the original file was copied back, the witness file was deleted, and `git status --short` was empty at HEAD 7740fc354. The restored command passed 6 times. The scratch worktree was removed (`git worktree list` no longer shows it).

## Recognition, not a new decision
This matches the execution retrospective's outcome-review observation. There are two hold mechanisms. `holdNextNotes` delivers its stale answer at cleanup and is safe only because nothing settles between ending holds and unmounting. Nothing pins that, and the probe confirms that an `await` there would push stale notes into the ending board without a maintained check noticing on the `holdNextNotes` path. The probe adds no repair decision. Repair and routing stay with the caller.

## Cost
- **Test runtime.** 119.0 s (measured), the sum of Vitest-reported `Duration` over 18 runs: 15 runs of the focused command plus 3 witness runs. The Vitest figure covers only the mounted share. The whole focused command, including Playwright startup, took 19.5 s wall time at baseline (measured, host clock).
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part during the probe and there is no separate measure.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable. There is no separately supported token or active-time measure for this agent run.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 406369 ms (measured), from 1795045917598 to 1795046323967 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision `7740fc354ff8f89eb2a8de63243792950fd6c6d8`. Verdict: Insufficient evidence for key example 4 (a held notes answer at case end; the next case opens clean). Decision: the gap fits the queued retrospective correction [Hold and settle mounted frontend cases by one rule](seeds/SEED-404-run-dashboard-frontend-checks-at-doughnut-speed.md#hold-and-settle-mounted-frontend-cases-by-one-rule) ([plan](slice-plans/711-hold-and-settle-mounted-frontend-cases/PLAN.md)). Its slice 1 now owns a kept-hold isolation case, the settle-before-unmount discrimination, and the cause of the connection-banner flip seen once in 7 faulted runs. One queue entry; no separate correction. The scratch fault is not evidence of a delivered defect: 7 unfaulted runs passed.
